teile.einleitung: The Federal Roads Office, FEDRO for short (in German ASTRA), is responsible for Switzerland's motorways. It plans, builds and maintains the national roads, on which a great many cars and lorries travel every day. It also makes rules for road traffic and vehicles.
wichtigste: FEDRO is the Federal Roads Office and belongs to the department DETEC.
It owns and runs the national roads, that is, the motorways and expressways.
In 1958 the people and the cantons approved the constitutional article on national roads.
In 1962 the Grauholz motorway near Bern opened as the first section of the N1.
FEDRO is based in Ittigen near Bern.
It also deals with traffic rules, vehicle regulations and road safety.
Anyone driving on Swiss motorways needs a vignette.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Roads Office** was founded in 1998 and is part of the Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications. It is based in Ittigen on the edge of the city of Bern. It is responsible for the **national roads**, that is, the network of motorways and important expressways. Since 2008 these roads have belonged entirely to the federal government and no longer to the cantons.

In 1958 the people and the cantons voted yes to a constitutional article on national roads. After that, a whole motorway network was planned. The first section of the national road N1, the **Grauholz motorway** near Bern, opened in 1962. Many more stretches were added later, including the Gotthard road tunnel, almost 17 kilometres long, in 1980.

The national road network has several thousand kilometres of carriageway and many tunnels and bridges. FEDRO has damaged road surfaces renewed, tunnels refurbished and bottlenecks widened. A big project is the **second bore** at the Gotthard, so that the old tunnel can be refurbished later. This is paid for, among other things, with money from the vignette and the mineral oil tax on petrol and diesel.

FEDRO draws up the **traffic rules** that apply to all roads. It also decides which regulations apply to cars, bicycles or e-scooters. This includes the Via sicura programme, with which the federal government wants to reduce the number of road deaths. FEDRO also collects figures on accidents in order to identify dangerous spots.

Anyone who drives a car on a Swiss motorway needs a **vignette**. It costs 40 francs a year and, since 2023, can also be bought electronically. Traffic management centres watch the traffic round the clock. When there are jams or accidents, they can change speed limits or close lanes.

begriffe.erklaerung: A road that belongs to the federal government, for example a motorway.
A yearly charge that allows you to use the motorways.
Changes to the constitution need a majority of voters and a majority of the cantons.
A single tunnel through which the carriageway runs.

gewusst: The very first stretch of motorway in Switzerland was already in use near Lucerne in 1955 but was not yet part of the national road network.
When it opened in 1980, the Gotthard road tunnel was the longest road tunnel in the world.
FEDRO is also responsible for the rules on how to get a driving licence in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office of Communications, OFCOM for short (in German BAKOM), looks after radio, television, telephone, mobile phones and the internet in Switzerland. It makes sure that everyone in the country can communicate well. Without its work, radio signals, for example, would interfere with each other.
wichtigste: OFCOM is a federal office in the Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications (DETEC).
It is based in Biel/Bienne in the canton of Bern.
It regulates radio and television in Switzerland.
It manages the radio frequencies that mobile phones, radios and Wi-Fi need.
It is responsible for Swiss telephone numbers and the internet ending .ch.
It makes sure that emergency numbers such as 112, 117, 118 and 144 work everywhere.
It supervises the collection of the radio and television fee.

abschnitte.text: OFCOM is a specialist office of the **federal administration**. It belongs to the department DETEC, which is headed by a member of the Federal Council. Its headquarters is in Biel/Bienne, a bilingual town on Lake Biel. The office prepares laws, grants licences and checks that the rules are followed. Important foundations are the **Telecommunications Act** and the Radio and Television Act.

OFCOM makes sure that there are radio and television programmes in all parts of the country. SRG SSR receives a **licence** from the Federal Council, that is, permission with a mission, to broadcast programmes in all the national languages. Many local radio stations and regional television channels also receive licences and money from the fee. Every household in Switzerland pays a **radio and television fee**, which is collected by the company Serafe. OFCOM supervises this system.

Mobile phones, radios, Wi-Fi, aviation radio and even garage door openers send signals with invisible **radio waves**. Each use needs its own band, a so-called **frequency**. If two devices send on the same frequency, they interfere with each other. That is why OFCOM shares out the frequencies and tracks down interference with measuring vans. The frequencies for the 5G mobile network were allocated to the mobile providers in an auction in 2019.

OFCOM manages Swiss **telephone numbers**, which begin with the country code +41. It is also responsible for the internet ending **.ch**. It also decides which basic services, the so-called universal service, must be offered everywhere in Switzerland. These include a telephone connection and internet access with a minimum speed, even in remote mountain villages. Some of these tasks are carried out together with the Federal Communications Commission ComCom.

OFCOM makes sure that emergency calls always get through, whichever provider you use. The most important numbers are 117 for the police, 118 for the fire brigade, 144 for the ambulance service and the European **emergency number** 112. The number 147 for children and young people in difficulty is also a protected short number. The office also looks after the security of the communication networks. In disasters, telephone and radio should keep working as far as possible.

begriffe.erklaerung: Official permission with a mission, for example to broadcast a radio programme.
A particular band of radio waves on which a device sends and receives.
Telephone and internet services that must be available everywhere in Switzerland.
The law that regulates telephone, mobile phones and the internet in Switzerland.

gewusst: OFCOM has measuring vehicles with which it can track down illegal transmitters and radio interference.
The internet ending .ch stands for Confoederatio Helvetica, the Latin name of Switzerland.
Because Biel/Bienne is bilingual, it is a fitting home for an office that connects all parts of the country.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH, in German BAG) is the federal government's most important health authority. It protects the population from diseases, issues vaccination recommendations and supervises health insurance. Many people got to know it during the coronavirus pandemic.
wichtigste: The FOPH belongs to the Federal Department of Home Affairs (FDHA) and is based in Bern.
It publishes the official Swiss vaccination schedule.
The FOPH supervises compulsory health insurance and approves the premiums.
According to the FOPH, all cantons except Ticino count as risk areas for the tick-borne disease TBE.
The TBE vaccination is generally recommended from the age of 3.
The most common tick-borne disease in Switzerland is Lyme disease.
The FOPH also deals with radiation protection, chemicals and addiction prevention.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Office of Public Health** is a federal authority based in Bern. It belongs to the **Federal Department of Home Affairs** (FDHA). Together with the cantons, it looks after the health of the population. The FOPH prepares laws, monitors infectious diseases and informs the public. The hospitals and doctors' surgeries themselves, on the other hand, are mainly a matter for the cantons.

Together with an expert commission, the FOPH publishes the official **Swiss vaccination schedule**. It says which vaccinations are recommended at which age. Doctors must report certain infectious diseases to the FOPH so that outbreaks are noticed early. During the **coronavirus pandemic** from 2020, the FOPH published figures and protective rules every day. Campaigns on flu, measles or AIDS also come from the FOPH.

Ticks can pass on dangerous diseases, most often **Lyme disease**. The disease **TBE**, an inflammation of the brain and its membranes caused by viruses, can be prevented with a vaccination. According to the FOPH, all cantons except Ticino count as TBE risk areas, and the vaccination is generally recommended from the age of 3. In the woods you should stay on wide paths, avoid undergrowth and check your body for ticks afterwards. The free app “Zecke”, developed at ZHAW with the support of the FOPH, helps with this.

In Switzerland everyone must take out **basic insurance** with a health insurance fund. The FOPH supervises this insurance and approves the **premiums** every year. It also decides which treatments and medicines the basic insurance must pay for. The new premiums for the following year are announced each autumn. They are an important topic in many families.

The FOPH also deals with **radiation protection**, for example in X-rays or with the radioactive gas radon in basements. It regulates the handling of dangerous **chemicals**. Another area is the prevention of addiction, for example to alcohol, tobacco or drugs. Campaigns are meant to help people live healthily. The FOPH also works with the World Health Organization WHO, which has its headquarters in Geneva.

begriffe.erklaerung: A list of which vaccinations are recommended at which age.
Tick-borne encephalitis, a viral inflammation of the brain passed on by ticks.
The amount you pay regularly to the health insurance fund.
Measures that prevent diseases before they arise.

gewusst: Ticks do not jump from trees; they usually wait on grass and bushes for people and animals to brush past.
There is no vaccination against Lyme disease, but there is one against TBE.
The World Health Organization WHO has its headquarters in Geneva.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office for Civil Protection (FOCP, in German BABS) makes sure that people in Switzerland are protected in disasters and emergencies. It looks after sirens, shelters and civil defence. The FOCP is based in Bern.
wichtigste: The FOCP belongs to the Federal Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport (DDPS).
It prepares Switzerland for disasters such as earthquakes, floods or power cuts.
The FOCP is responsible for the sirens and for alerting the population.
Every year in February, the nationwide siren test takes place.
The National Emergency Operations Centre and the Spiez Laboratory belong to the FOCP.
The Alertswiss app gives information about warnings and alarms.
In Switzerland there is a place in a shelter for almost every inhabitant.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Office for Civil Protection** is a federal authority based in Bern. It belongs to the **DDPS**, the Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport. Its task is to protect the population from disasters and emergencies. These include natural events such as earthquakes, floods or avalanches, but also power cuts, pandemics or accidents in nuclear power stations. The FOCP works closely with the cantons.

**Civil protection** in Switzerland is a network of five partners. They are the police, the fire brigade, the health services, the technical services and **civil defence**. In a major event they work together under one command. The federal government sets the rules, and the cantons are responsible for the work on the ground. The FOCP looks after training, planning and cooperation.

There are thousands of **sirens** all over Switzerland that warn the population of danger. When the “general alarm” sounds, a wailing tone that rises and falls, you should listen to the radio, follow the instructions and tell your neighbours. Every year on the first Wednesday in February, all sirens are checked in the **siren test**. In addition, the **Alertswiss** app sends warnings straight to your phone. The **National Emergency Operations Centre** in Zurich is staffed round the clock.

Switzerland has a special feature: there is a place in a **shelter** for almost every inhabitant. These rooms are usually in the basement of blocks of flats or in public buildings. They have thick concrete walls, heavy doors and ventilation with filters. Many were built during the Cold War. The FOCP sets out how shelters must be built and maintained.

The **Spiez Laboratory** in the Bernese Oberland belongs to the FOCP. There, experts examine dangerous chemical, biological and radioactive substances. The laboratory is also known internationally and helps, for example, with investigations into chemical weapons. The FOCP also looks after the **protection of cultural property**. This means protecting valuable buildings, works of art and archives from destruction in war or disasters.

begriffe.erklaerung: An organisation in which people doing protection service help in disasters.
An especially safe room, usually in the basement, that gives protection in danger.
The yearly check of all sirens on the first Wednesday in February.
Protecting valuable buildings, works of art and archives.

gewusst: Hardly any other country has as many shelter places for its population as Switzerland.
During the siren test in February, sirens wail all over Switzerland at the same time.
The “water alarm” sounds different from the general alarm and warns of danger from dams.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office of Topography, swisstopo for short, surveys Switzerland and draws its official maps. It knows exactly where every mountain, every river and every house is. The Swiss maps by swisstopo are thought to be especially beautiful and accurate all over the world.
wichtigste: swisstopo is responsible in Switzerland for the national survey and the official maps.
The office belongs to the Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport (DDPS).
It is based in Wabern near Bern.
Its roots go back to 1838, when Guillaume-Henri Dufour founded the Topographic Bureau.
Switzerland's highest peak, the Dufourspitze, is named after Dufour.
swisstopo also studies what lies beneath Switzerland's surface, that is, its geology.
All the maps can be viewed free of charge on the internet and in an app.

abschnitte.text: swisstopo is the federal specialist office for **geoinformation**, that is, all information about where something is. It belongs to the DDPS and is based in Wabern, a place in the municipality of Köniz near Bern. The office surveys the country, makes maps, takes aerial photographs and collects data on rock and soil. These data are needed, for example, by civil engineers, authorities, rescue services and hikers. Satnavs and apps also often use data from swisstopo.

In 1838 the Geneva general **Guillaume-Henri Dufour** founded the Federal Topographic Bureau. Under his leadership, the first accurate map of the whole of Switzerland was made at a scale of 1:100,000, the **Dufour map**. The work took many years; the sheets appeared from 1845 into the 1860s. The mountains were drawn on it with shading so that they look almost three-dimensional. In honour of Dufour, Switzerland's highest peak, in the Monte Rosa massif, was named the Dufourspitze; it is 4634 metres high.

For a map to be right, the country must first be surveyed precisely. For this there are thousands of **survey points** all over Switzerland whose position is known to the centimetre. Today satellites also help. Every place in Switzerland has its own **national coordinates**, which you can read off at the edge of every national map. The starting point for heights is a boulder in Lake Geneva, the Repère Pierre du Niton.

The best-known products are the **national maps** at various scales, for example 1:25,000 and 1:50,000. On a map at a scale of 1:25,000, one centimetre corresponds to 250 metres in reality. Typical of Swiss maps are the fine rock drawing and the shading, which make mountains look three-dimensional. The maps are updated regularly so that new roads and houses are shown. Today they can be viewed free of charge on map.geo.admin.ch or in the swisstopo app.

swisstopo is also Switzerland's **national geological survey**. It makes geological maps showing which rocks lie in the ground. In the Mont Terri rock laboratory in the canton of Jura, scientists study how rock behaves over very long periods. In addition, swisstopo aircraft regularly photograph Switzerland from above. This creates a huge archive of **aerial photographs**, in which you can see how villages and landscapes have changed.

begriffe.erklaerung: The description of the Earth's surface with its mountains, valleys, rivers and buildings.
Shows how much smaller a map is compared with reality.
Numbers that let you pinpoint a place on the map exactly.
Precisely measuring the position, size and height of land and buildings.

gewusst: In the past, cartographers secretly hid small drawings in the national maps, for example a marmot or a spider.
The Dufourspitze used to be called the Gornerhorn and got its present name in 1863.
With the swisstopo app you can see on your phone what an area looked like more than a hundred years ago.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office for the Environment, FOEN for short (in German BAFU), looks after nature and the environment in Switzerland. It works for clean water, healthy air, healthy forests and many animal and plant species. It also helps to protect people from natural hazards such as avalanches and floods.
wichtigste: The FOEN is the federal environment office and belongs to the department DETEC.
It is based in Ittigen near Bern and was created in 2006.
It deals with water, air, soil, forests, noise, waste and climate.
According to the FOEN's Red Lists, about a third of the species assessed in Switzerland are threatened (as of 2023).
About half of Switzerland's forest is protection forest.
Protection forest protects villages and roads from avalanches, rockfall and landslides.
The FOEN gives warnings about natural hazards such as floods.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Office for the Environment** is the federal specialist office for all environmental questions. It was created in 2006, when the former Federal Office for the Environment, Forests and Landscape was merged with parts of the Federal Office for Water and Geology. The FOEN belongs to DETEC and is based in Ittigen near Bern. It prepares laws and helps the cantons to put them into practice.

**Biodiversity**, that is, the variety of animals, plants and fungi, is an important task of the FOEN. The **Red Lists** show which species are endangered in Switzerland. About a third of the species assessed are considered threatened, especially species in wetlands and waters. That is why the FOEN supports protected areas, moors and floodplains.

About a third of Switzerland's area is covered with forest. About half of it is **protection forest**. On steep slopes this forest stops avalanches, rockfall and landslides and so protects villages, roads and railway lines. The FOEN makes sure that such forests are looked after and stay healthy.

The FOEN measures how high the water is and how clean it is in many rivers and lakes. When **floods** threaten, it issues warnings so that municipalities can prepare. It also supports protective structures such as embankments and avalanche barriers. Much of this information can be found on the federal natural hazards platform.

The FOEN monitors air quality and noise, for example along motorways. It is also responsible for **climate policy**, that is, measures against the warming of the Earth. It also sets rules for waste and recycling. The fact that Switzerland collects a lot of glass, PET and paper is partly due to these rules.

begriffe.erklaerung: The variety of all living things and their habitats.
A list that shows which animal and plant species are threatened.
Forest that protects people and buildings from avalanches, falling rocks and landslides.
A natural event such as a flood or an avalanche that can cause damage.

gewusst: A healthy protection forest can give as much protection as expensive avalanche barriers made of steel and concrete.
The FOEN runs measuring stations that report the water levels of rivers and lakes round the clock.
Protecting the wolf, the lynx and the beaver is also one of the FOEN's topics.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office of Culture, FOC for short (in German BAK), is the culture office of the Swiss Confederation. It supports art, film, music, literature and design and protects valuable buildings and cultural property. In this way it helps to keep Switzerland's varied culture alive.
wichtigste: The FOC belongs to the Federal Department of Home Affairs (FDHA) and is based in Bern.
It supports film-making and culture throughout Switzerland.
It deals with the care of historic monuments, heritage protection and archaeology.
The Swiss National Library in Bern belongs to the FOC.
It awards Swiss prizes for art, design, film, literature, music and theatre.
It supports the national languages, especially Romansh and Italian.
The federal government sets the goals of its cultural policy for four years at a time in the culture message.

abschnitte.text: The FOC is a federal office in the **Department of Home Affairs**. In Switzerland, culture is mainly the responsibility of the cantons and municipalities. The federal government takes on tasks that are important for the whole country. How the federal government supports culture is set out every four years in the **culture message**, which Parliament decides on. The FOC carries out these plans and works closely with the Pro Helvetia foundation.

A large part of the money goes to **film-making**. The FOC supports Swiss feature films, documentaries and animated films so that they can be made at all. Every year the Swiss Film Award is presented. There are also Swiss prizes for art, design, literature, music, theatre and dance. In this way artists become better known and can make a living from their work.

The FOC helps to preserve old castles, churches, bridges and townscapes. For this it pays contributions to the **care of historic monuments** and to archaeological excavations. It keeps the federal inventory of townscapes worth protecting, ISOS for short. It also makes sure that no stolen or looted **cultural property** is brought into Switzerland or sold here. World Heritage Sites such as the Old City of Bern or the Abbey of St Gallen are also close to its heart.

The **Swiss National Library** in Bern belongs to the FOC. It collects everything published in Switzerland or about Switzerland, that is, books, newspapers, posters and much more. The FOC also looks after some museums, for example the Museum of Musical Automatons in Seewen in the canton of Solothurn and the Museo Vela in Ticino. It also manages the federal art collection with many thousands of works. Many of them hang on loan in museums and embassies.

Switzerland has four national languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh. The FOC supports **multilingualism** and exchange between the language regions. Romansh in the Grisons and Italian in Ticino and the southern Grisons receive special support. The culture of the Yenish and Sinti, who live as Travellers, is also supported. The FOC also promotes reading and the musical education of children and young people.

begriffe.erklaerung: A federal plan that sets out for four years how culture will be supported.
The work of preserving old and valuable buildings.
An object or building that is important for history and culture.
When several languages are spoken in a country or by one person.

gewusst: The National Library has to collect not only books but also archive Swiss websites.
The Museum of Musical Automatons in Seewen has music boxes and organs that make music without any musicians.
In Switzerland the cantons, towns and municipalities together spend much more money on culture than the federal government.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Social Insurance Office, FSIO for short (in German BSV), looks after social security in Switzerland. It is responsible for the AVS, disability insurance and many other insurance schemes that protect people in old age, illness or accident. Family and youth policy is also one of its tasks.
wichtigste: The FSIO belongs to the Federal Department of Home Affairs (FDHA) and is based in Bern.
The AVS was introduced in 1948 and is financed mainly on a pay-as-you-go basis.
Since 1972 the three-pillar principle of pension provision has been set out in the Federal Constitution.
The AVS contribution rate is 8.7 per cent of the wage, paid half each by employer and employee (as of 2026).
In occupational pension provision a minimum conversion rate of 6.8 per cent applies (as of 2026).
Pillar 3a belongs to the third pillar, private pension provision.
The FSIO runs the national platform Youth and Media to promote media skills.

abschnitte.text: The FSIO is the federal specialist office for **social insurance**. It belongs to the Department of Home Affairs and prepares laws, for example reforms of the AVS. It also checks that the insurance schemes work properly. However, pensions are not paid out by the FSIO itself but by the **compensation offices** and the disability insurance offices. Besides pension provision, the FSIO looks after families, children and young people.

Old-age and survivors' insurance, **AVS** for short, was introduced in 1948. It pays pensions to older people and to widows, widowers and orphans. It is financed mainly on a **pay-as-you-go basis**: today's workers' contributions directly pay today's pensions. The contribution is 8.7 per cent of gross pay, that is, pay before any deductions, and the employer pays half of it. The normal retirement age is 65; for women it is being raised step by step from 64 to 65.

Since 1972 the **three-pillar principle** has been in the Federal Constitution. The first pillar is the AVS together with disability insurance; it is meant to cover basic needs. The second pillar is **occupational pension provision** with the pension funds, into which employees and employers pay together. On retirement, the savings are converted into a pension using the conversion rate, at least 6.8 per cent in the compulsory part. The third pillar is private pension provision, for example tax-favoured saving in pillar 3a.

**Disability insurance** (IV) has existed since 1960. It helps people who can no longer work, or can only work part of the time, because of an illness or an accident. The income compensation scheme replaces part of the wage, for example during military service or maternity. Supplementary benefits help when the pension is not enough to live on. Compulsory health insurance is now looked after by the Federal Office of Public Health; the lowest standard deductible for adults is 300 francs (as of 2026).

The FSIO is also responsible for **family allowances**, that is, money that parents receive for their children. It supports work with children and young people and is committed to protecting children. With the **Youth and Media** platform, it helps children, young people, parents and teachers to use mobile phones, the internet and games safely and wisely. There are tips on topics such as screen time, cyberbullying and data protection. In this way the FSIO combines social security with support in everyday life.

begriffe.erklaerung: State insurance that helps people in old age, illness, accident or unemployment.
Today's workers' contributions directly pay today's pensions.
Pay before deductions such as AVS contributions are taken off.
The amount you pay yourself each year before the health insurance fund pays.
The percentage used to convert pension fund savings into a yearly pension.

gewusst: Everyone who lives or works in Switzerland gets their own AVS number, which begins with 756.
In 2024 the Swiss people voted for a 13th AVS pension payment, which will be paid once a year in addition from 2026.
Even students without an income have to pay AVS contributions from the age of 21.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office of Sport, FOSPO for short (in German BASPO), is the federal body that looks after sport and exercise in Switzerland. Its headquarters is in Magglingen, high above Lake Biel. Perhaps you have taken part in a Youth+Sport camp yourself, which FOSPO supports.
wichtigste: FOSPO is Switzerland's Federal Office of Sport.
Its headquarters is in Magglingen above Biel in the canton of Bern.
It belongs to the Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport (DDPS).
Its most important support programme is called Youth+Sport and is meant for children and young people aged 5 to 20.
The Swiss Federal Institute of Sport Magglingen belongs to FOSPO.
In Tenero in Ticino, FOSPO runs a large sports centre for young people.
FOSPO also works for fair, clean sport without doping.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Office of Sport** is a section of the federal administration. It belongs to the DDPS, which is also home to the army and civil protection. Its task is to promote sport and exercise for everyone in Switzerland. This includes grassroots sport for everyone as well as top-level sport.

The headquarters is in **Magglingen**, a place on a sunny terrace above Biel and Lake Biel. There are sports halls, grass pitches, an athletics ground and accommodation for training camps. The Federal Gymnastics and Sports School was founded here as early as 1944. A second important site is the youth sports centre in **Tenero** on Lake Maggiore, where school classes and clubs can hold camps.

**Youth+Sport**, J+S for short, is the federal government's largest sports support programme. It is aimed at children and young people aged 5 to 20. Clubs and schools receive federal money if they offer courses and camps with trained leaders. J+S has existed since 1972, and today hundreds of thousands of children take part every year in many sports, from football to mountaineering.

The **Swiss Federal Institute of Sport Magglingen**, SFISM for short, belongs to FOSPO. There you can, for example, study sports science or train as a coach. Researchers study how to train better and how exercise strengthens health. Leaders for J+S are also trained according to FOSPO's guidelines.

Together with the umbrella organisation Swiss Olympic, FOSPO supports Swiss top-level sport. For athletes in the army there are even special elite sport recruit schools. The office also works for **fair play** and against doping. The doping tests themselves are carried out by the independent foundation Swiss Sport Integrity.

begriffe.erklaerung: A specialist office of the federal administration that deals with a particular subject.
A federal programme that supports sports courses and camps for 5- to 20-year-olds.
Sport that many people do in their free time, not just professionals.
Banned substances or methods used to boost your own performance artificially.

gewusst: In French Magglingen is called Macolin, and FOSPO is known there in both languages.
Many Swiss Olympic athletes have trained in Magglingen.
Anyone who wants to lead a J+S camp needs special training for it.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Statistical Office, FSO for short (in German BFS), collects figures about Switzerland and its population. It knows, for example, how many people live here, how many children are born and how fast prices are rising. It is based in Neuchâtel.
wichtigste: The FSO is the federal government's central statistics office and is based in Neuchâtel.
It belongs to the Federal Department of Home Affairs (FDHA).
At the end of 2024, about a quarter of the permanent resident population did not have a Swiss passport.
In 2024 the birth rate was about 1.3 children per woman.
The FSO calculates the Swiss consumer price index, which measures inflation.
For statistics, the FSO divides Switzerland into 7 major regions.
Its figures help politics, business and schools to make good decisions.

abschnitte.text: The FSO collects, checks and publishes **statistics** on almost every area of life. These include population, work, health, education, transport, the environment and elections. The figures often come from the registers of municipalities and cantons or from surveys. Anyone can look at the results free of charge on the internet.

Federal statistics began in 1860 with the Federal Statistical Bureau in Bern. Since 1998 the federal office has been housed in **Neuchâtel**, in a modern building near the station. In the past, a large **census** was held every ten years, in which every household filled in a questionnaire. Since 2010 the FSO has instead mainly used registers and yearly sample surveys.

At the end of 2024, about 9 million people lived in Switzerland. About a quarter of them did not have a Swiss passport. In 2024 the **birth rate** was about 1.3 children per woman, which is very low compared with the past. The most common cause of death is heart and circulatory disease, as the statistics for 2022 show.

Every month the FSO calculates the **Swiss consumer price index**, CPI for short. To do this, it follows how the prices of a typical basket of goods, including bread, rents, clothes and much more, change. The FSO also shows that over 99 per cent of Swiss companies are SMEs with fewer than 250 employees, namely about 99.7 per cent in 2021. The quarterly estimates of gross domestic product, however, are published by SECO.

The FSO also analyses elections and votes. In the 2023 National Council elections, **turnout** was about 47 per cent. So that areas can be compared, the FSO divides Switzerland into 7 major regions, such as the Lake Geneva region, Espace Mittelland or Ticino. In this way you can compare, for example, where more people travel to work by train.

begriffe.erklaerung: Collecting and analysing lots of figures in order to see something general.
When goods and services become more expensive on average.
The average number of children a woman has during her life.
A selection of people who are surveyed instead of asking everyone.

gewusst: The FSO does not survey everyone; for the structural survey it asks only a sample of about 200,000 people each year.
From the FSO's figures we even know which first names are most popular for babies in Switzerland.
A turnout of about 47 per cent means that fewer than half of those entitled to vote actually voted.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office of Transport, FOT for short (in German BAV), is the federal specialist office for public transport. It looks after trains, buses, trams, boats and cable cars. Thanks to its work, people in Switzerland can get almost anywhere by public transport.
wichtigste: The FOT is the Federal Office of Transport and belongs to the department DETEC.
It is based in Ittigen near Bern.
It is responsible for rail, buses, trams, boats and cable cars.
The FOT plans the expansion of the rail network and distributes federal money for it.
It monitors safety in public transport.
At 57 kilometres, the Gotthard Base Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world.
Switzerland is one of the countries where people travel by train the most.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Office of Transport** belongs to the Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications. It is based in Ittigen near Bern. It is responsible for **public transport**, that is, means of transport that everyone can use. These include railways, PostBuses, trams, boats on the lakes and cable cars in the mountains.

Together with the railway companies, the FOT plans how the network will be expanded in the future. Since 2016 the money for this has come from the **Railway Infrastructure Fund**, which voters approved in 2014. It pays for new tracks, stations and tunnels and for maintaining existing facilities. The aim is for more trains to run and for connections to fit together well.

A major project was the **New Railway Link through the Alps**, NRLA for short. It includes the Lötschberg Base Tunnel from 2007, the Gotthard Base Tunnel from 2016 and the Ceneri Base Tunnel from 2020. At 57 kilometres, the Gotthard Base Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world. The NRLA is meant above all to help carry goods through the Alps by rail instead of by lorry.

The FOT is also a **supervisory authority**. It checks that railways, buses and cable cars are built and run safely. New vehicles and installations need a permit from the FOT before they may carry passengers. After an accident, the office can demand improvements.

Many bus routes and regional trains in the countryside would not pay for themselves. That is why the federal government and the cantons together pay part of the costs, so that even small villages stay connected. The FOT orders such services in **regional transport** together with the cantons. In this way, for example, the PostBus also runs into remote mountain valleys.

begriffe.erklaerung: Means of transport such as trains, buses and trams that anyone may use with a ticket.
New Railway Link through the Alps, a building project with long railway tunnels through the Alps.
A body that checks whether rules are being followed.
A pot of money intended for a particular purpose.

gewusst: Work on building the Gotthard Base Tunnel went on for about 17 years.
Chairlifts and gondola lifts in ski resorts also need a federal permit.
A large part of the freight traffic through the Swiss Alps goes by rail instead of by road.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss Federal Office of Energy (SFOE, in German BFE) is the federal government's specialist authority for all questions about energy. It makes sure that Switzerland is supplied with energy that is secure, affordable and environmentally friendly. The SFOE is based in Ittigen near Bern.
wichtigste: The SFOE belongs to the Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications (DETEC).
It is based in Ittigen near Bern.
In May 2017 voters approved the Energy Strategy 2050, with a ban on new nuclear power stations.
The SFOE carries out this energy strategy.
In 2024 hydropower supplied about 60 per cent of the country's own electricity production.
With the SwissEnergy programme, the SFOE gives information about saving energy and renewable energy.
The SFOE also monitors the safety of large dams.

abschnitte.text: The **Swiss Federal Office of Energy** is an authority of the federal administration. It belongs to **DETEC**, the Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications. It is based in Ittigen near Bern. The SFOE prepares laws and rules on energy and advises the Federal Council. It also collects figures on the production and use of energy in Switzerland.

In May 2017 Swiss voters approved the **Energy Strategy 2050**. It bans the building of new nuclear power stations and promotes renewable energy and saving energy. The SFOE is responsible for carrying out this strategy. This includes subsidies for solar installations and other renewable power stations. Another aim is that by 2050 Switzerland should no longer emit any greenhouse gases overall; this is called **net zero**.

Every year the SFOE publishes the **electricity statistics**. From these we know, for example, that in 2024 hydropower supplied about 60 per cent of the country's own electricity production. The second-largest share comes from nuclear power stations. Solar electricity is growing especially fast. In winter Switzerland often has to **import** electricity from abroad; in summer it often exports.

Through the **SwissEnergy** programme, the SFOE has given tips on saving energy and on renewable energy since 2001. It supports municipalities, companies and schools with projects. The SFOE is also responsible for the **energy label**, which shows on appliances and cars how economical they are. During the threatened energy shortage in winter 2022/23, the federal government called on people to save. Many people lowered the room temperature or switched off lights at that time.

The SFOE monitors the safety of large **dams** and reservoirs, for example the Grande Dixence. It is also involved in planning power lines and grids. In the search for a site for a **deep repository** for radioactive waste, the SFOE leads the process. The safety of the nuclear power stations themselves, however, is supervised by the independent ENSI. In this way several bodies share the responsibility.

begriffe.erklaerung: The Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications, to which the SFOE belongs.
Switzerland's plan for a secure and climate-friendly energy supply.
The aim of no longer emitting any additional greenhouse gases overall.
A coloured label that shows how much energy an appliance uses.

gewusst: Switzerland has more than 200 large dams, which are checked regularly.
In winter Switzerland needs more electricity than it produces itself and therefore often imports from neighbouring countries.
Every year the SFOE keeps statistics on how much energy Switzerland uses.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office for Agriculture, FOAG for short (in German BLW), looks after Swiss farms and their work. It makes sure that food is produced in Switzerland while nature is protected. For this it pays out billions of francs to farmers every year.
wichtigste: The FOAG belongs to the Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research (EAER) and is based in Bern.
It carries out the federal government's agricultural policy.
Farms receive direct payments from the federal government for their services.
To receive direct payments, they must provide the proof of ecological performance (PEP).
Under the PEP, as a rule at least 7 per cent of the farmland must be biodiversity promotion areas.
The FOAG protects specialities such as Gruyère with the labels AOP and IGP.
The tasks of agriculture are set out in Article 104 of the Federal Constitution.

abschnitte.text: The FOAG is the federal specialist office for **agriculture**. It belongs to the EAER and works closely with the research institute Agroscope. It prepares laws and ordinances and pays money out to farms. Its basis is the Agriculture Act. According to the **Federal Constitution**, agriculture should supply the population with food, preserve nature, look after the landscape and help to keep even remote areas settled.

Swiss farms often could not survive from selling their products alone, because costs are high. That is why they receive **direct payments** from the federal government, about 2.8 billion francs a year in total. These pay for services to the community, for example looking after mountain meadows or especially animal-friendly stables. Those who do more for nature and animals get extra contributions. The FOAG sets the rules, and the cantons check the farms.

To receive direct payments, a farm must provide the **proof of ecological performance**, PEP for short. This includes keeping farm animals in a way that suits them and a balanced use of fertiliser. Fields must be farmed in a set crop rotation so that the soil stays healthy. As a rule, at least 7 per cent of the area must be **biodiversity promotion areas**, such as flower meadows, hedges or traditional orchards with tall fruit trees. There, insects, birds and other animals find a habitat.

The FOAG keeps a register of protected designations of origin. **AOP** marks a product that is made entirely in its region of origin, for example Gruyère, Emmentaler or Raclette du Valais. **IGP** means that at least one step of production takes place in the region, for example with Bündnerfleisch or the St Gallen bratwurst. This means others cannot simply copy these names. The FOAG also regulates what may be sold as organic.

To protect home-grown agriculture, Switzerland charges **customs duties** on many imported foods. The FOAG helps decide how much of a product may be imported at a lower duty. The number of farms has been falling for decades; in 2023 there were still about 48,000. At the same time, individual farms are getting bigger. Important questions for the future are climate change, fewer plant protection products and healthy soils.

begriffe.erklaerung: The rules and goals with which the state steers agriculture.
Money from the federal government to farms for services to nature and society.
The variety of animals, plants and habitats.
A protected designation of origin for products that come entirely from a particular region.

gewusst: Tall traditional fruit trees also count as a biodiversity promotion area, because many birds and insects live in them.
A large part of Switzerland's farmland is grassland, which is suited above all to cows, sheep and goats.
There are extra federal contributions for animals that are regularly allowed outdoors.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Office of Justice (FOJ, in German BJ) is the federal government's legal department. It helps to draft new laws, assists in cooperation with foreign authorities and keeps important registers. The FOJ is based in Bern.
wichtigste: The FOJ belongs to the Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP).
It prepares laws, for example in civil law, criminal law and constitutional law.
It checks whether new laws are compatible with the Federal Constitution.
The FOJ is responsible for international legal assistance and extraditions.
It keeps Switzerland's criminal record register.
The FOJ supervises the commercial register, in which companies are entered.
It helps with international child abductions and adoptions.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Office of Justice** is a federal authority based in Bern. It belongs to the **Federal Department of Justice and Police** (FDJP). You can think of it as the federal government's legal specialist office. Its lawyers advise the Federal Council and the other federal offices on legal questions. The FOJ is not a court and does not pass judgements.

An important task of the FOJ is **legislation**. It drafts new laws or changes, for example in the **Civil Code** or the **Criminal Code**. It also checks whether the laws are compatible with the Federal Constitution and international law. The drafts then go out for consultation, where cantons, parties and associations give their views. In the end the Federal Council and Parliament decide, and sometimes the people.

Criminals do not stop at national borders. That is why the FOJ works with foreign authorities on **international legal assistance**. For example, it decides on **extraditions** of wanted persons. It also helps to exchange evidence or stolen money between countries. In cases of children being abducted abroad, the FOJ is Switzerland's central point of contact.

The FOJ keeps the Swiss **criminal record register**, in which convictions are entered. Anyone starting a job working with children, for example, sometimes has to show an extract from it. The FOJ also supervises the **commercial register**, in which all the companies in Switzerland are listed. It also regulates civil status matters, where births, marriages and deaths are recorded. These registers ensure order and legal certainty.

The FOJ is the central authority for **international adoptions** and checks that the rights of the child are respected. It supports victims of crime with rules on victim support. The federal government also pays contributions through the FOJ for building prisons and for measures for young people. It also follows how the law develops in other countries. In this way the FOJ helps the **rule of law** to work well.

begriffe.erklaerung: Drafting and passing laws.
Cooperation between authorities of different countries in criminal proceedings.
Handing over a wanted person to another country for criminal proceedings.
A register in which people's convictions are entered.
A state in which everyone, including the government, is bound by the law.

gewusst: The Swiss Civil Code came into force in 1912 and still applies today in revised form.
Anyone founding a company in Switzerland can have it entered in the commercial register, which anyone can look at.
The FOJ often works on laws that the whole population later votes on.
